title: IBM, Mitsubishi Chemical, and Keio Train Generative Quantum Eigensolvers on 70-Qubit Hardware - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IBM, Mitsubishi Chemical, Keio University and NVIDIA trained transformer-based Generative Quantum Eigensolver policies directly on the 156-qubit IBM Heron ibm_kobe, then applied them zero-shot to 56-70 qubit organotin EUV photoresist simulations with 64-160 two-qubit gates versus 4,248-6,952 for LUCJ, landing 27 of 28 runs within 15 mHa of DMRG.

insights.claim: Hardware-trained Generative Quantum Eigensolver policies generated circuits with 64-160 two-qubit gates at 56-70 qubits, versus 4,248-6,952 gates for a transpiled LUCJ baseline.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: ~40x+ gate reductions make chemistry circuits viable on noisy hardware now, not just after fault tolerance.
insights.locator: 70-Qubit GQE-SQD vs. Conventional LUCJ Ansatz Performance

insights.claim: GQE-generated circuits had transpiled depths of 44-134 layers versus 428-536 layers for the LUCJ baseline.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shallower circuits reduce decoherence exposure, raising result quality per QPU dollar.
insights.locator: 70-Qubit GQE-SQD vs. Conventional LUCJ Ansatz Performance

insights.claim: At 46-70 qubits, 27 of 28 GQE-SQD runs landed within 15 mHa of DMRG references (median 4.5 mHa), while LUCJ showed 22.7-204.1 mHa raw deviation before excitation injection.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Approaching classical-reference accuracy on industrially relevant molecules is a credibility milestone for quantum chemistry.
insights.locator: 70-Qubit GQE-SQD vs. Conventional LUCJ Ansatz Performance

insights.claim: The consortium used a two-stage reinforcement learning curriculum: pre-training on a noiseless simulator across transition-metal complexes, then continued training on the IBM Heron ibm_kobe processor across 46- and 70-qubit active spaces.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: AI-generated circuits trained in hardware loop are an emerging alternative to hand-designed ansatze.

insights.claim: Stage-2 hardware training added a reward penalty to prevent policy collapse onto the classical Hartree-Fock state and consumed 120 million physical hardware shots across 600 calibration jobs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Training is QPU-hungry upfront, which is a revenue driver for hardware providers, but amortized at inference.
insights.quote: consuming 120 million physical hardware shots across 600 calibration jobs

insights.claim: In inference, the GQE policy proposes ten candidate circuits run in a single quantum batch job; a classical ranking pass picks the best, and subspace recovery and diagonalization then run entirely on local GPUs with no further quantum time.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Minimal QPU time per inference with GPU-heavy post-processing favors hybrid quantum-GPU vendors such as NVIDIA.

insights.claim: IBM, Mitsubishi Chemical, Keio University and NVIDIA applied hardware-trained GQE policies zero-shot to 11 active-space tiers of methyltin trihydroxide and its mono- and di-hydrates, organotin photoresist molecules for EUV lithography.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Targeting semiconductor-lithography materials ties quantum chemistry to a high-value industrial supply chain.

insights.claim: Under sample-based quantum diagonalization, state-preparation quality determines recovery accuracy, but conventional ansatze often produce prohibitive gate depths once mapped to physical hardware topologies.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Identifies state preparation as the binding constraint, where AI-designed circuits create edge.
